To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HIV-1 RT mutation M184 V suppresses the excision of chain terminating nucleotides by HIV-1 RT containing thymidine analogue resistant mutations (TAM) to a greater degree when the template is RNA than when the template is DNA.

1) the M184V RT mutation suppressed the excison of AZTMP from a DNA template to the same extent as from an RNA template; 2) this suppression was not due to the M184V effect on RT binding to AZTMP; 3) the M184 V mutation suppressed the excition of AZTMP by increasing RNase H cleavages at −7 relative to AZTMP; and 4) the K65R RT mutation suppressed the AZTMP excision activity

(1) The excision of chain-terminating AZTMP is suppressed more effectively on an RNA template by HIV-1 RT containing the M184V resistance mutation than on a DNA sequence of the same sequence, but this effect is not seen with RT containing the K65R resistance mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of M184V suppression and suggests a role for template cleavage in reduced excision of AZT by RT containing TAMs.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M184V suppression is not a result of a direct effect of the mutation on the excision reaction.
M184V suppresses the excision activity by reducing the binding of reverse transcriptase to the template-primer complex and by reducing the cleavage of the template-primer at position −7.
M184V suppresses the excision activity by increasing the cleavage of the template near the primer termini.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the M184V suppresses AZT resistance through the enhancement of the RNase H activity, which leads to increased primer-template separation and reduced excision of AZT monophosphate.
M184V suppression is a consequence of the reduced stability of the RT-primer/template complex and is independent of the nature of the primer terminus.

(1) M184V reduces excision of 2′,3′-dideoxynucleotides (ddNs) on an RNA template, but not on a DNA template, (2) the reduced excision activity is associated with enhanced RNase H activity, and (3) the enhancement of RNase H activity is associated with the dissociation and reassociation of RT at the −7 site.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of M184V in HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (HIV-RT) suppresses the excision of chain-terminating 3′-azide thymidine (AZT) nucleotide triphosphates (NTPs) on a RNA template to a greater extent than it does on a DNA template.

M184V suppresses the excision of chain-terminating 3TC and AZT nucleotides by human immunodeficiency (HIV) RT to a greater extent when the nucleoside analog is incorporated into an RNA template than when it is incorporated into a DNA template.
the M184V and K65R mutations suppress AZTMP excision through distinct mechanisms.
